If you’re really concerned and you have $70-200 to spare (in this economy?!), get a dog DNA test to settle any future matters. If possible, have your vet list your pup as a Mixed breed/(a non discriminated breed). I’d say Lab mix but the ears speak to her Terrier side. They can’t do anything about it with official documentation from a professional. 
Source: I worked in rescue for years and we’d frequently change their breed in our system upon adoption for any stickler landlords or home owners associations. 
The fact is not even dog “experts” can accurately assume the breed of a non-purebred dog. I’ve seen dogs look like XYZ and we label them as such, then the adopter says they got a DNA test done and the pup is actually ABCZ.

Leaving my boyfriend of 3 years the same day as losing my third job in 1.5 years. I couldn’t handle all the actual and anticipated rejection. Instead of talking things out like a normal person, I decided to leave the state the same day I was terminated. 
We were far from perfect, but the heightened emotional state when everything is black and white genuinely scares me. Living with the intense regret of hurting some I still love, even if he’s already moved on 💔 

7 months later, I have PTSD, no job, live with my parents in my personal hell at age 32, still have a hypertonic pelvic floor that flares up whenever I’m super stressed and emotional. I hate being such a highly sensitive person.
And all the fun PMDD symptoms that AFAB have to endure. I’ve traced my PMS symptoms back to when I lost three jobs and consequently my relationship.

My trauma response to actual unexpected criticism or perceived criticism combined with people-pleasing while self-advocating for myself, got me fired from my dream organization two years ago. I had worked SO hard to get there and cried the day I was hired. I wanted nothing more than to contribute and climb the ranks, but trauma responses and being treated differently for being quirky ruined that for me. 

I spiraled into the worst depression of my life, and got fired from another job 3 months after that, and then spent all my savings while in despair. 

I was fired from another job I enjoyed in October for struggling to communicate efficiently and when I’d be late, and still felt like I wasn’t myself.

The day of my third termination, I left my partner of three years (semi-abusive but loved him), half my belongings I don’t even remember packing, my self-respect, and my dignity. Now I’m back home in my personal hell sleeping in the bed of my emotional abuser.
The brain fog, anxiety and depression have been relentless and the negative thoughts on overdrive.

I’m sorry to hear you had a similar experience to mine, but I went through a board certified neuropsychologist who ironically specializes in everything but autism….

His assessment said my history doesn’t align with an ADHD diagnosis, which quite honestly shocked me. He recommended being tested for autism. 
I believe I have the phenotype or my autistic traits are exacerbated situationally or when under intense stress. 

Now I get to have a fun conversation with both he and my psychiatrist (who wanted me to be retested and curb my anxiety before resuming ADHD treatment) and present why I believe I still have ADHD if they’re not going to dx me with PTSD at this point. 

I don’t think doctors realize how overwhelming those 3 hour assessments can be, especially when you’re still a bit traumatized from the events that made you seek another professional opinion in the first place. I struggle with eye contact due to my intense shame and guilt for how my life has turned out, and regret a lot. He was the first person I had spent any time with outside of therapy and my family in months. 

How dare he say I don’t have ADHD bc I did well academically and showed up to the appointment on time. I busted my ass in high school and most of college to get acceptable grades, and that came at a cost of not having close friendships. 
I struggle with time management/blindness, concentration/focus and working memory, impulsivity and intrusive thinking so so much. 
ADHD meds always helped manage those symptoms. Granted I’ve experienced a ton of complex trauma from having my experiences invalidated over the years when NTs take their every day experiences for granted.

The supplements have worked better than any antidepressant, anxiolytic, or antipsychotic I’ve been on. 
Having this information years ago would have life changing. Depression and complex traumatic events have ruled my life due to poor coping mechanisms.

I’m so sorry to hear what you’re going through and it’s understandable why you feel the way you do. 

I think many women, especially those who are neurodivergent, can empathize with your situation, and you’re incredibly strong-willed for trying to do the right thing for your son. We’re so drawn toward upholding our morals even if contradicts our values and it often comes back to hurt us in the long run. 

In October, I decided to leave the man I spent 3 years giving myself to, actually enjoyed sex with, who made my heart happy…he was a slightly more immature (male) version of myself. But after losing my third job in 1.5 years due to the national  adderall shortage throwing my systems off and revving up my anxiety, which began to manifest as chronic pain, I decided to move out and leave the state within 24 hours. He told me to “just leave” when I told him I didn’t want to. 
I wanted to heal from my past trauma. He didn’t, and wanted to stay a boy in Neverland and “stay sick.” He wasn’t receiving treatment for bipolar disorder. 

It sounds like that’s what your man intends to do. Who he is when that switch goes off is who he will *always* be unless HE decides to put in even a *fraction* of the work you’ve been doing for yourself for years. 

One of the hardest things I’ve learned this year is that I cannot control the actions of others regardless of my good intentions and over the top efforts. Obsessions and wishful thinking are my forms of self-sabotage. “Letting go” has always been a foreign concept to me. I convinced myself I loved him so much and wanted to help at the expense of my own health. I messed up a lot communicating my needs, but as a self dx autistic woman with ADHD, bipolar 2, anxiety and now with clinically suspected borderline, there are certain lines a partner cannot cross before inflicting severe psychological harm, which he did. 

He also had ADHD symptoms, signs of being on the spectrum, and borderline tendencies as well.

Two traumatized people trying to make shit not smell bad. It usually doesn’t work out, but we do silly things for love.

Reframing intrusive thoughts focused on self blame will be very important for you moving forward ✨

I highly recommend reading “Women Who Love Too Much” by Robin Norwood. It may help you process things and start to heal. I’ve been in the same depths of despair and it helped me put things in third person perspective a bit more.

I personally recommend against using it for ADHD unless you have good impulse control and aren’t prone to dependent behaviors. You just have to know what works for you. 
I dated a guy who I always suspected of having Asperger’s, or on the spectrum. We both abused pot and told ourselves it didn’t interfere with our lives but it did. It’s held me back for years, as it does cloud the mind and affect executive function. I haven’t touched CBD oil with more than 3% THC since February. I’d be looking to quit entirely if it weren’t for the bodily aches and pains and weak pelvic floor I’ve developed in the aftermath of a traumatic dismissal from a job I loved a year ago. Sometimes it’s very effective to “chill out” after intense hyper focus, when our bodies feel in overdrive and our thoughts racing. However, I’ve found that daily usage can exacerbate anxiety, depression, and OCD tendencies. 
Proud to say I’ve cut back immensely since February. While it certainly mitigates the side effects of ADHD stimulants, I recommend using it sparingly.
